headline: Indonesian Nickel Reference Prices Increase Amid Declining Gold
seoTitle: Nickel Prices Rise as Indonesian Gold Valuation Falls
metaDescription: Indonesian nickel reference prices have reached over US$15,500 per ton, while gold prices continue to record consistent declines in regional markets.
aiSummaryBullets: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources reported that nickel reference prices increased to US$15,596 per ton for late November 2026.
Nickel prices experienced a recorded growth of four percent for the month of November.
Market data indicates a simultaneous downward trend for gold prices across major domestic brands including Antam and UBS.
aiContextParagraph: As of mid-November 2026, the Indonesian commodity market shows divergent trends between base metals and precious metals. The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources confirmed that the reference price for nickel has ascended to US$15,596 per ton, marking a four percent increase throughout the month. This upward movement contrasts with the performance of the gold sector, where prices for various brands, including Antam and those tracked by Pegadaian, have consistently depreciated. Reports indicate that the valuation of gold per gram has dropped, impacting both standard purchase rates and buyback values. These adjustments follow recent broader economic fluctuations, including shifts in international oil prices and national debt levels documented during the third quarter of 2026. Market observers are monitoring these commodity variations as they influence local trade and investment sentiment within the country.
whyItIsViral: This story is trending due to coverage from five independent media outlets reporting on significant price shifts in major Indonesian commodities.
